partners.mechanism_chain: FGFR3 activating mutation (rs12345678) —DISRUPTS→ FGFR3 (HGNC:3672); FGFR3 (HGNC:3672) —LEADS_TO→ FGFR3 signaling pathway (WP:WP478); FGFR3 signaling pathway (WP:WP478) —INCREASES→ Eosinophilia (HP:0001880); FGFR3 signaling pathway (WP:WP478) —INCREASES→ Epidermal hyperplasia (HP:0030105). Activating mutations (e.g., in the kinase domain) in FGFR3 lead to its constitutive activation, driving downstream signaling pathways. In the epidermis, the same aberrant FGFR3 signaling promotes keratinocyte proliferation, leading to epidermal hyperplasia seen in epidermal nevi.

partners.mechanism_chain: IL2RG (HGNC:6079) —DISRUPTS→ Cytokine Signaling Pathway (GO:0007165); Cytokine Signaling Pathway (GO:0007165) —LEADS_TO→ JAK-STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242) —DECREASES→ Eosinophilia (HP:0001890); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242) —DECREASES→ Severe combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002718); Severe combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002718) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormalities of B cell function (HP:0002691); Severe combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002718) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormalities of T cell function (HP:0002693). Loss-of-function mutations in IL2RG disrupt cytokine signaling pathways, including the JAK-STAT pathway. This disruption leads to a decrease in normal T and B cell development and function, causing severe combined immunodeficiency. Concurrently, altered cytokine signaling due to IL2RG deficiency can lead to dysregulation of other immune cell populations, such as eosinophils, resulting in eosinophilia characteristic of some forms of hypereosinophilic syndrome.

falsification.text: The identification of pathogenic variants in IL2RG in patients with idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome that are distinct from those causing T-B+ SCID, and which do not affect the shared cytokine signaling pathways in a way that explains both phenotypes, would falsify this hypothesis. #### 1. polyps, multiple and recurrent inflammatory fibroid, gastrointestinal  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.730)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5673001, Reactome:R-HSA-9674396, Reactome:R-HSA-9674401, Reactome:R-HSA-9674403, Reactome:R-HSA-9674428)

Gain-of-function mutations in PDGFRA lead to aberrant activation of the MAPK signaling pathway, which in turn promotes uncontrolled cell proliferation and survival. This dysregulation manifests as eosinophilia in idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome and gastrointestinal polyps in inflammatory fibroid polyps.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in PDGFRA with loss-of-function effects in patients with either idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome or gastrointestinal inflammatory fibroid polyps would falsify this gain-of-function hypothesis. _(variant: rs769695602)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting PDGFRA signaling could offer a unified therapeutic strategy for both idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome and gastrointestinal inflammatory fibroid polyps, potentially improving patient outcomes by simultaneously addressing the underlying molecular drivers of both conditions.
